envelope.text: **`ErrorCode::Unsupported` under a manual kind on a backend with no

why:
phase-428 W6 remainder (2026-09-06), CLOSED and re-verdicted 2026-09-25 (the phase-467 RMW gap-closure design study's Row 7). Was `gap`/`adopt`; the behavioural half it was open for is fixed, and what remains is the return type, which IS a platform constraint.

THE DIVERGENCE: `rclcpp::PublisherBase::assert_liveliness()` returns `bool`; ours (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/publisher.hpp`) returns `Result`. RFC-0018 — no exceptions — so a verdict richer than yes/no travels in the return value. The widening is LOUD: `Result` is `[[nodiscard]]`-shaped, and `if (pub->assert_liveliness())` inverts against `Result`'s truthiness rather than compiling wrong. Worth checking at the call site; it is the ordinary RFC-0018 widening and nothing more.

WHAT THE ROW WAS ACTUALLY OPEN FOR, and what happened to it. phase-428 W5 RANKED-15 recorded that on zenoh this call produced NO WIRE TRAFFIC while returning `Ok(())` — "one question, four answers" across the backends, with the header documenting a fifth. A `Result::ok` from a call that asserted nothing is the silently-wrong shape RFC-0089 Part I is about, and the return type being wider does not fix it.

The 2026-09-23 re-read left it open. The phase-467 study MEASURED the four answers and found the row's own framing too generous to one backend and too harsh to another:
  * **cyclonedds IMPLEMENTS it** — `dds_assert_liveliness` on the writer, gated on the entity's manual kind (`packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/publisher.cpp`). It renews the lease and sends a Heartbeat. So this was never "the API is wrong"; it was one backend's answer.
  * **zenoh-pico cannot.** Its liveliness is a SESSION-scoped keepalive; a per-topic lease a call can renew is a DDS concept the transport does not have. Re-declaring the `@ros2_lv` token on every assert was the alternative and is worse than silence — a peer reads the churn as leave/join.

THE FIX, and it is per backend rather than per API: under a kind for which `QoSLivelinessPolicy::is_manual` holds, a backend with no per-topic lease answers `Unsupported` — which `rmw_vtable.h` has prescribed since phase 108. zenoh-pico, XRCE-DDS and uORB now do. Under `AUTOMATIC` / `NONE` every backend answers `Ok`, because there was nothing to assert; that half was ALSO unimplemented — the `nros-rmw-cffi` NULL-slot arm answered `Unsupported` whatever the caller had asked for, and its own comment said "the runtime caller (Node) gates the call by liveliness_kind", which `EmbeddedPublisher::assert_liveliness` does not do and never did.

zenoh's LOCAL watchdog survives on purpose: `assert_liveliness` still stamps `last_assert_at_ms`, and `check_liveliness_lost` still fires this publisher's own `LivelinessLost` when the gap exceeds the lease. Recording the call and reporting `Unsupported` is not a contradiction — the return value is about what a PEER can see.

The per-backend table lives in `docs/reference/platform-implementation-notes.md`, because the divergence belongs to the backends and not to the API. The C and C++ entry points propagate it (`rcl_publisher_assert_liveliness` answers `RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED`; `nros_cpp_publisher_assert_liveliness` goes through `transport_error_to_cpp_ret`, which it did not before — it flattened every error to `NROS_CPP_RET_ERROR`). Tests: `packages/rmw/cffi/tests/publisher_gid.rs`.
